FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Secondary Cells and Batteries Sectional Committee has been approved by the Electrotechnical Division 
Council. 


This standard was first published in 1995 to address need for standardization of batteries for motor vehicles having 
high engine compression ratios and fuel efficiency that require high cranking current. This revision incorporates 
the experience gained with the use of this standard and brings the standard in line with the latest developments in 
this field. 


The major changes in this standard include the following: 
IN 88 battery type incorporated in Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7. 
b) Polarity marking details incorporated under 8.3

c) Caution symbol details incorporated under 8.4 


d) Cold Cranking Performance Test (CCA) removed from Annex B. It is included as electrical performance 
requirement under 9.3.6. CCA values incorporated in Table 4. CCA test incorporated in sequence of tests. 


e 


wm 


Reserve capacity test removed from Annex B. It is included as electrical performance requirement under 
9.3.7. Reserve capacities for all battery types incorporated in Table 4. reserve capacity incorporated in 
sequence of tests. 


f) Water consumption test included in main body of specification under 9.3.9. Water consumption test 
incorporated in sequence of tests. 


g) Charge retention test included in main body of specification under 9.3.10. Charge retention test 
incorporated in sequence of tests.

Light load endurance test included in main body of specification under 9.3.11. Light load endurance 
requirements for all battery types incorporated in Table 4. Light load endurance test incorporated in 
sequence of tests.

Electrolyte retention test included in main body of specification under 9.3.14. Electrolyte retention test 
incorporated in sequence of tests. 


k) Robustness of handle test (B-1.1) and residual capacity test (B-1.2) incorporated as special tests in 
Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 14257 : 2019 


Indian Standard 


LEAD-ACID STORAGE BATTERIES FOR MOTOR 
VEHICLES WITH LIGHT WEIGHT AND HIGH 
CRANKING PERFORMANCE — SPECIFICATION 
( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers characteristics, dimensions and 
tests for light weight lead acid storage batteries with 
12 V rated voltage to be used for starting and meeting 
other electrical load of vehicles driven by internal 
combustion engines. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards indicated in Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in IS 1885 (Part 15) in addition to the following shall 


apply. 


3.1 Type Tests — Tests carried out to prove conformity 
with the requirements given in the standard. These are 
intended to prove the general quality and design of a 
given type of battery. 


3.2 Acceptance Tests — Tests carried out on samples 
selected from a lot to verify the acceptability of the lot. 


3.3 Dry Charged Batteries — A battery intended for 
use as soon as it has been filled with electrolyte, without 
any initial charging or alternatively with additional 
activation charging according to manufacturer’s 
recommendations. 


4 MATERIALS, 
WORKMANSHIP 


CONSTRUCTION AND 


4.0 General Construction 


The battery consists of six elements connected in 
series and housed in a plastic monobloccontainer. Each 
element consists of positive plates, negative plates and 
separators. The lid with one positive and one negative 
terminal shall be sealed to the container by heat sealing 
or ultrasonic sealing or by adhesion with sealing 
material. 


4.1 Container and Lid 

The container and lid shall be of plastic, such as 
polypropylene, ABS, etc, conforming to IS 1146. 

4.2 Separator 

Separators shall be leaf or envelope type, with or 
without glassmat conforming to IS 6071. 

4.3 Sealing Material 


Sealing material employed shall be an acid resistant 
adhesive, wherever the sealing is not heat sealing or 
ultrasonic welding. 


4.4 Terminals 


The terminals shall be made of lead alloys and shall 
conform in shape and dimensions to Fig. 1 and Table1. 


All dimensions in millimeters

4.5 Electrolyte 


The sulphuricacid and water used for the preparation 
and maintenance of electrolyte shall conform to 
IS 266 and IS 1069 respectively. 


4.6 Specific Gravity 


Tests are to be carried out on a fully charged battery 
having electrolyte at maximum level and specific 
gravity1.280 0.01 (corrected to 27°C). 

The temperature correction shall be made by using 
following formula: 


SG,, = SG, + 0.0007 (t-27) 


Where, 
SG, = specific gravity at 27°C, 
SG, = specific gravity at t°C, and 
t = temperature of electrolyte at the 
time of measurement, °C. 
5 RATING 


High performance storage batteries shall be rated at Sh 
rate and the ratings shall be chosen from Table 2. 


The 5h rating is the ampere-hour obtained when the 
battery is discharged at a constant current I = 0.2 C, A 
down to a final terminal voltage of 10.50 V, the capacity 
being corrected to an electrolyte temperature of 27°C 
(see 9.3.4.1). 


6 CAPACITIES, DIMENSIONS, MASS AND 
LAYOUT 


Capacities, overall dimension and mass (with 
electrolyte of 1.280 + 0.01 specific gravity at 27°C) 
shall conform to Table 2. 


The layout of the battery and polarity of the terminals 
shall conform to either Fig. 2 or Fig. 3 as indicated in 
Table 2. 


7 CHARGING 


7.1 The initial and normal charging of batteries 
shall be done in accordance with the manufacturer’s 
instructions. 


7.2 Fully Charged Battery 


A battery is deemed to be fully charged when the 
terminal voltage and specific gravity of electrolyte 
(corrected for temperature) measured every 30 min 
towards end of charging at the recommended current 
shows a constant value 3 times consecutively. 


8 MARKING 


8.1 The following information shall be marked on the 
battery at easily visible places: 


a) Indication of source of manufacture, 

b) Type, 

c) Country of manufacture, and 

d) Manufacturing batch code: 3% digit will be 


manufacturing month code and 4" digit will be 
manufacturing year code. 


8.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and 
Regulations framed thereunder, and the products may 
be marked with the standard mark.

8.3 Polarity Marking 


The polarity shall be marked at least for the positive 
terminal. For marking, “+” mark shall be shown on the 
upper surface of the lid near the positive terminal or on 
the positive terminal. While marking negative polarity, 
“—” mark shall be shown on the upper surface of the lid 
near the negative terminal or on the negative terminal. 


8.4 Caution Symbol 


On batteries, six coloured symbols as shown in Fig. 
A and symbols shown in Fig. C and Fig. D shall be 
marked. The minimum size of symbols shall be 10 mm 
(see Fig. B). Symbols are collectively marked on the 
upper surface of the battery.

9.2 Equipment 


9.2.1 Voltmeter and Ammeter 


The voltmeter and ammeter used shall be of an accuracy 
class not inferior to 0.5 in accordance with IS 1248 
(Part 2). 


9.2.2 Thermometer 


A thermometer with an appropriate scale shall be 
used for measuring temperature and one division of 
graduated scale shall represent at the most 1°C. The 
accuracy of the calibration shall be not less than 
0.5°C. 


9.2.3 Hydrometer 


The specific gravity of the electrolyte shall be measured 
by a hydrometer provided with a graduated scale, one 
division of which shall represent at the most 0.005 unit 
of specific gravity. The accuracy of calibration shall be 
not less than 0.005 unit of specific gravity. 


9.2.4 Instrument for Measuring Length 


For measuring overall dimensions, a calliper or metal 
ruler shall be used of an accuracy not inferior to 
0.5 mm. 


9.3 Methods of Test and Requirements 


9.3.1 Physical Examination 


The batteries shall be checked for conformity with the 
requirements of 4 for type tests. 


For acceptance tests, the batteries shall be checked for 
conformance to 4.0 and 4.4 only. 

9.3.2 Dimensions and Layout 

The dimensions and layout shall be checked for 
conformance to Table 2. 

9.3.3 Marking 

The batteries shall be checked by visual inspection for 
conformity with 8. 

9.3.4 Capacity (5 h Rate) Test 


The 5h capacity shall be determined by discharging a 
fully charged battery (see 7.1) at a constant current of 
I=0.2 C, amperes to a final terminal voltage of 10.50 V

9.3.4.1 Temperature correction test 


The capacity obtained by multiplying the discharge 
current in amperes by the discharge duration in hours 
shall be corrected to the standard reference temperature 
27°C as follows: 


Ct 
Cn = 1+0.01 (t-27) 
where, 
C,, = 5h capacity at an average electrolyte temperature 
of 27°C; 
C, = 5h capacity at an average electrolyte temperature 
t; and 
t = mean of initial and final electrolyte temperature, 
im °C. 
9.3.4.2 Requirement 


Batteries tested shall reach the rated 5 h capacity during 
the course of the first three cycles after initial charge. 
Alternatively, the battery will be deemed to have passed 
the capacity test if it meets 95 percent of the rated 5 h 
capacity in the first discharge. 


9.3.5 High Rate Discharge Test 


The high rate discharge is tested at —15°C under the 
following conditions: 


a) Before a high rate discharge test, the battery shall 
be subjected to a 5 h capacity test. 

b) The batteries under test shall comply with the 
conditions given in Table 3. 

c) The battery shall be discharged at the current 
specified against its type in Table 4 down to a 
terminal voltage of 6.00 V. The terminal voltage 
shall be taken at 5 s to 7 s and at 30 s intervals 


thereafter.

NOTE — If the battery fails to reach the values specified in 9.3.6 Cold Cranking Performance Test (CCA) 
Table 4, two more tests may be carried out up to a total of three 


high rate discharges. The cold cranking performance is a measure of cranking 


abilities of a battery at —18°C. The Cold Cranking 
Ampere (CCA) test shall be conducted on a battery that 
has passed 5 h capacity test as per 9.3.4. 


a) CCA test to be conducted on a fully charged 
battery. 


b) Battery shall be placed in a cooling chamber at a 
temperature —18°C + 1°C for a minimum period 
of 24 h or until temperature of electrolyte of either 
cell in the centre position stabilizes at —18°C + 
1°C. 

Discharge the battery at the rating current. 
The rating current shall be held constant + 1 A 
throughout the discharge. Battery terminal voltage 
shall be measured under load at the end of 30 s.

d 


Ww 


The acceptance criteria of this test is that battery 
terminal voltage at 30 s shall be equivalent to 7.2V 
or more. 


9.3.7 Reserve Capacity Test 


The reserve capacity is the period of time in minutes 
for which a fully charged battery can maintain a 
discharge current of 25 A to a cut-off voltage 10.5 V at 
a temperature 25°C + 2°C. 


a) Throughout the test, the battery shall be placed 
in a water bath at 25°C + 2°C. The water surface 
shall be 15 mm to 25 mm below the upper surface 
of the battery. If several batteries are in the same 
water bath then the distance between them and 
also the distance to the walls of the bath shall be at 
least 25 mm. 


b 


wm 


After completion of charging, confirm that 
electrolyte temperature of either cell in the 
centre position is 25°C + 2°C. Then the battery 
shall be discharged with current of 25 A + 1 
percent until the terminal voltage falls to 10.5 
V + 0.05 V. The duration ¢ (min) of discharging 
shall be recorded. 


Record the electrolyte temperature T°C at end 
of discharge, and calculate the effective reserve 
capacity C, „using following formula : 


C, = t [1 — 0.009 (7 — 25)] (min) 


c 


s 


where, 
C.. = Effective reserve capacity, Min ; 
t = Duration of discharge (min); and 
T = Electrolyte temperature (°C). 
9.3.7.1 Requirement 
The battery shall meet the minimum requirement given 
in Table 4.

9.3.9 Water Consumption Test 


a) After completion of charging, clean and dry the 
surface of battery and weigh the mass of battery 
(W1) with an accuracy of +0.05 percent or lower. 


b) Battery shall be placed in a water bath at a 
temperature of 40°C + 2°C. The water surface 
shall be 15 mm to 25 mm below the upper surface 
of the battery. If several batteries are in the same 
water bath then distance between them and also 
the distance from the walls of the bath shall be at 
least 25 mm. 


c) Charge the battery with constant voltage of 14.40 
V + 0.05 V for a period of 500 h. 


d) Immediately after overcharge, clean and dry the 
surface of battery and weigh the mass of battery 
(W2). 

e) Water Consumption calculated as: 

[((WI-W2)/1.2429]C_ 2^5 (g/Ah) 


Where, 

C., - Effective reserve capacity, in minutes. 
9.3.9.1 Requirement 
For small water consumption battery : 4 g/Ah 


For very small water consumption battery : 1 g/Ah 


IS 14257 : 2019 


9.3.10 Charge Retention Test 


a) A battery with its vent plugs firmly in place and 
a clean, dry surface shall be stored at 40°C + 
2°C for the following period in open circuit. No 
connecting clamps or cables shall be attached to 
the terminal during storage. 


For small water consumption battery : 14 days 


For very small water consumption battery : 49 
days 
b 


wm 


After the storage period, without recharge, the 
battery shall be placed in a cooling chamber at 
a temperature of —18°C + 1°C for a minimum of 
20 h or until the temperature of either cell in the 
centre position has reached —18°C + 1°C. 


c 


wa 


The battery shall be discharged within 2 min after 
the cooling with 0.6I,, , i.e. 0.6 times the nominal 
cold cranking current. Discharge current shall be 
kept constant within 0.61, + 0.5 percent. 


9.3.10.1 Requirement 


The terminal voltage after 30 s from start of discharge 
shall be 8.0 V or more. 


9.3.11 Light Load Endurance (LLE) Test 


a) Throughout the test, the battery shall be placed in 
water bath at a temperature 41°C + 3°C. The water 
surface shall be 15 mm to 25 mm below the upper 
surface of the battery. If several batteries are in the 
same water bath, then the distance between them 
and also the distance to walls of the bath shall be 
at least 25 mm. 


b 


wn 


Connect the battery to the endurance test 

equipment and repeat discharge and charge cycles 

as given below : 

1) Discharging : Battery shall be discharged for 
240s +1 s at a current of 25 A+0.1A 

2) Charging : Battery shall be charged for 600s + 
1 s at a voltage of 14.8V + 0.03V 

(limit current 25 A+ 0.1 A) 

c) At every 480 cycles, battery shall be left for 56 h. 

d) Battery shall be discharged with nominal cranking 

current for 30 s at LLE test temperature and 

voltage shall be recorded. 


Requirement: Voltage after 30 s of discharge shall be 
not less than 7.2V. 


e) Then, the battery shall be charged as stated in 
9.3.11 [b(ii)]. 
The number of runs until the endurance is defined by 


the number of cycles in which the voltage after 30 s 
becomes 7.2 V. 


f) Water filling shall be done appropriately with 
pure water during the test. However, topping up 
shall not be done immediately before the checking 
discharges. 


9.3.12 Life Cycle Test 


The life cycle test is carried out on a battery which has 
passed the test of 9.3.4 and 9.3.5. 


a) Throughout the test and during the checking 
discharges, the battery shall be kept at an ambient 
temperature (in a water bath or environmental test 
chamber) of 40°C to 45°C. 


The battery shall be subjected to a series of 
discharges and charges as in Table 5. 


During the test, at the 25", 50", 75" and every 
25" cycle thereafter, a continuous discharge shall 
be made at the current in Table 5, S1 No. (i) until 
terminal voltage drops down to 10.20 V and the 
corresponding duration is to be measured. 


b 


wm 


c

wa 


The test is terminated when the capacity obtained 
as the product of discharge time (at 40 to 45°C 
ambient) and the discharge current falls to 50 
percent or less of the Sh capacity in Table 2 and 
does not increase again. 


e 


mn 


After every checking discharge (c) the battery shall 
be recharged at the appropriate current in Table 5, 
SI No. (ii) until the specific gravity (corrected to 
27°C) and terminal voltage is constant for three 
consecutive 30 min readings. 


f) Throughout the test, the level of electrolyte shall 
be maintained at the specified level by topping 
up with pure water. Topping up should be done 
during the charging portion of cycles. The battery 
shall not be topped up immediately before the 
checking discharges (c). 


ae 


The number of life cycles is determined graphically 
from a curve of number of cycles (X-axis) against 
capacity (Y-axis). 

The number of tests at 5h rate (9.3.4) and high rate 
discharge (9.3.5) shall be added to the number of life 
cycles obtained graphically above. 


8 


9.3.12.1 Requirement 


The battery shall meet the minimum requirements 
given in Table 4. 


9.3.13 Overcharge Endurance Test 
The overcharge endurance test is conducted on a 


battery which has passed the test of 9.3.4 and 9.3.5 and 
has been fully charged. 


a) Throughout the test the battery shall be kept 
at an ambient temperature (in a water bath or 
environmental test chamber of 40°C to 45°C). 

b) The battery shall be charged at the appropriate 
current given in Table 6 for a period of 110 h. 

c) The battery is then allowed to stand for 48 h on 
open circuit after (b). 

d) At the end of the open circuit stand (c), the battery 


is to be discharged at the appropriate current in 
Table 6, SI No. (ii) for 30 s.

e) The procedure (b), (c) and (d) constitute one 
overcharge endurance cycle. Immediately after 
(d), the battery shall be subjected to the next cycle 
of overcharge without recharging. 


f) When the terminal voltage of the battery reaches 
down to 7.2 V before 30 s in the test (d), 
the overcharge endurance test is terminated and the 
battery is deemed to have reached the end of its 
overcharge endurance. 


During the test the battery shall be periodically 
topped up with pure water to maintain the correct 
electrolyte level. 


g) 


9.3.13.1 Requirement 


The battery shall meet the number of overcharge 
endurance cycles specified in Table 4, the number 
excluding the last cycle in which the discharge duration 
was less than 30 s. 


9.3.14 Electrolyte Retention Test 


a) Charged battery shall be placed in open circuit at a 
temperature of 25°C 5°C for 4 h. 

b) If required, electrolyte level of each cell will be 
adjusted to the maximum level with pure water. 
The surface of battery shall be cleaned and dried. 


c) Battery shall be tilted in back forth and both sides. 
Each test given below shall be performed at an 
interval of 30s or more. 


1) Battery shall be tilted at 45° from upright 
position within a period of 1s. 


2) Maintain in tilted position for 3s. 
3) Battery shall be back to upright position within 
a period of Is. 
9.3.14.1 Requirement 
After the test, no evidence of liquid shall visible on 
vent plugs. 
9.3.15 Vibration Resistance Test 


The resistance to vibration is conducted on a fully 
charged battery after it has passed a capacity test 
(9.3.4). The battery is tested under the following 
conditions: 


a) Discharge current during vibration = 0.2 C, A, 


b) Direction of vibration = vertical simple harmonic 
motion, 


c) Peak to peak amplitude = 2.3 to 2.5 mm, 
d) Acceleration = 3g (29.4 m/s’), and 
e) Duration of vibration = 2 h.

9.3.15.1 Requirement 


There shall be no abnormality or sudden drop in voltage 
or spillage of electrolyte exhibited by the battery during 
the test. 
NOTE — In the absence of suitable test facilities to carry 
out the vibration test as specified above and providing that 
purchaser agrees, the vibration test can be carried out as 
specified. 


9.3.15.1.1 The test shall be performed in accordance 
with IS 9000 (Part 8). The samples shall be first tested 
for capacity test at 20h rate before putting into vibration 
test. The test consists in vibrating the batteries at a 
frequency of 16 Hz with a total displacement of 5 mm 
for a period of 2 h. During vibration the batteries shall 
be discharged at the 20h rate. 


9.3.16 Strength of Terminal Test 


The strength of terminal is tested by fitting suitable 
adoptors to the positive and negative terminals (see 
Fig. 4), and applying a torque to the adopter by means 
of a torque wrench in the direction of rotation illustrated 
in Fig. 5. 
The torque applied shall be as follows: 

a) 11.8 Nm for small terminals (Table 1),and 

b) 14.7 Nm for standard terminals (Table 1). 


9.3.16.1 Requirement 


The battery terminals shall withstand the torque applied 
without breaking off or exhibiting any abnormality.

9.3.17 Robustness to Fastening Test 
The robustness to fastening is tested under the following 
conditions: 

a) Fastening is made at ambient temperature, 


b) During the test the temperature shall be kept 
between 60°C to 65°C, and 
c) The duration of test is 5 h after fastening. During 
this period and after test the state of the battery is 
examined. 
The battery is fastened vertically, diagonally or 
horizontally in accordance with the method given 
in Table 7. The individual fastening procedures are 
illustrated in Fig. 6 to Fig. 8. 


9.3.17.1 Requirement 


There shall be no visual deformation in the battery 
during the test. 


NOTE — This test is optional and shall be carried out only if 
specifically asked for by the purchaser.

9.3.18 Test for Dry-Charged Battery 


9.3.18.1 The battery shall be tested within 60 days of 
manufacture. 


9.3.18.2 The battery shall be maintained at a temperature 
of 27°C + 2°C for 24 h prior to test. 


11 


9.3.18.3 The battery shall then be filled with electrolyte 
of specific gravity 1.280 + 0.01. The temperature of the 
electrolyte before filling shall be 27°C + 2°C. 


9.3.18.4 20 minutes after completion of filling, the 
battery shall be discharged at a constant current I = 
0.2 C, until the terminal voltage has fallen to 10.5 V. 
Reading during the discharge and the calculation of 
capacity shall be noted as 9.3.4. 


9.3.18.5 Requirements 
The battery shall give not less than 80 percent of its 
rated 5 h capacity. 


NOTE — This test is applicable to those batteries which have 
been declared as ‘dry-charged’ by the manufacturer.

ANNEX B 
( Clause 9.1.1.1) 


SPECIAL TESTS 


B-1 If the contract between manufacturer and customer 
specially calls for, the following special tests may be 
conducted: 


a) Robustness of handles (B-1.1), and 
b) Residual capacity test (B-1.2). 


B-1.1 Robustness of Handles Test 


The handles shall be such that they cannot be detached 
accidentally from the battery during use or handling. 
To determine the robustness of handle or both handles 
(in case of two handles), either of the following tests 
to be conducted. Generally procedure 1 is followed by 
the manufacturer unless any special requirement by the 
customer. 


B-1.1.1 Procedure 1 


a) A load equal to three times of the weight of the 
battery is attached to the handle or both handles 
(in case of two handles), and shall be lifted with 
a lifting device to a height of one meter with a 
speed of 0.2 m/s followed by smooth lowering. 
The process shall be repeated for five times. 


b) Then battery shall be left hanging for 1 h. 


13 


B-1.1.2 Procedure 2 


a) An equal load to the weight of the battery is 
attached to the handle or both handles (in case 
of two handles), and shall be lifted with a lifting 
device to a height of one meter with a speed of 
0.2 m/sec followed by smooth lowering. 

b) Then battery shall be left hanging minimum for 
6h. 


B-1.1.3 Requirement 


After the test, no bending or breaking of the handles 
shall be observed. 


B-1.2 Residual Capacity Test 
a) This test shall be performed on a battery within 
60 days from last date of charging. 


b) The battery shall be discharged with the constant 
current I, down to a final discharge voltage of 
10.50 V. 


c) The capacity shall be measured at 27 + 2°C. 


B-1.2.1 Requirement 


Residual capacity shall be 65 percent minimum of rated 
capacity. 


IS 14257 : 2019 


ANNEX C 
( Clause 9.1.3 ) 


SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR ACCEPTANCE 


C-1 LOT 


All the batteries of the same type, design and rating, 
manufactured by the same factory during the same 
period using the same process and materials offered for 
inspection at a time shall constitute a lot. 


C-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING 


The number of batteries to be selected at random from 
the lot shall be in accordance with col | and 2 of Table 8. 


In order to ensure the randomness for selection random 
number tables shall be used (see IS 4905). 


The batteries selected shall be subjected to the 
acceptance tests in the order specified in 9.1.2. 


Each of the battery selected in the first stage in 
accordance with col 2 of Table 8 shall be tested for 
acceptance. A battery shall be declared defective if 
it fails in one or more of the acceptance tests. If the 
number of defects is less than or equal to C1 the lot 
shall be considered as conforming to the requirements 
of the standard. If the number of defects is equal to or 
less than C2 and greater than Cl, a further sample of 
same size as taken in the first stage shall be taken and 
tested. If the number of defectives in the two samples 
combined is less than C3 the lot shall be considered 
as conforming to the requirements of this standard 
otherwise the lot shall be considered as not conforming 
to the requirements of the standard.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: ETD 11 (11295).
